parsed.explanation: Combined regime: this state/province offers documented operating protections for state facilities, services and care, but federal rules the state cannot pre-empt impose birth-sex passport/federal-facility policy, discrepancy-based entry refusal with possible fraud ineligibility, and federal custody care removal. If outed at the border or in federal custody, state protections do not follow; if the traveller remains in state services, protections do operate. National litigation, funding pressure and unresolved ballot constraints make remedies partial.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex policy; X-marker processing stopped for national passports, existing X valid to expiry. Entry cable: document/record discrepancy or reasonable doubt on sex requires refusal and more evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility, requiring four elements and not automatic. Passports reported confiscated/blocked for trans travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Litigation by civil-liberties union on behalf of seven plaintiffs; several orders blocked/enjoined; legal-aid FAQ on documents. No documented general acceptance guarantee for foreign X/mismatched passports.
entry_documents.interaction: State marker-change ease does not govern foreign passports or federal entry. A discrepancy can move visitor from entry to refusal, investigation and possible fraud finding, overriding state protection.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections from 2026 adopted model described as conversion therapy: short haircuts, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; care denial reported and trans prisoner counts stopped. Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse reported for trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State custody: 2024 consent decree requires expanded healthcare, voluntary 100-bed specialised housing at men's prison, integration unit at women's prison, about $2.1m to roughly 400 members; earlier $170,000 settlement.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State decree mitigates state prisons only, not federal or immigration detention. Federal detention interaction can result in birth-sex/conversion-model placement and care denial despite state decree.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Nationally 9+1 units ban in all government buildings, others partial; 4 units make some use criminal under trespass circumstances, with one documented handcuffed arrest and 24 hours in men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province: 2013 ruling allowing trans child girls' restroom, 2023 law granting full bathroom access for all genders, anti-discrimination coverage since 2008 expanded 2025. It is among units with no mapped ban, though other sex-definition laws may affect access.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State law protects state/public accommodations but does not cancel federal facilities rule. Traveller can use state facilities by identity yet face exclusion in federal buildings within same state.

care_services.exposure: National funding freeze, October 2025 proposed rules barring public insurance for under-18 care, August 2026 national rule blocking funds noted as cause of state public-insurance suspension for youth from 13 Oct 2026, six-month taper only for existing youth patients. Border/medication seizure not documented.
care_services.protection: State 2023 law protects/defends gender-affirming care and safe passage; insurance must cover reassignment surgery since 2023; 18 May 2026 highest court 5-2 ordered hospital to resume puberty blockers/hormones after suspension under national pressure.
care_services.interaction: State court protection operates for state services but national funding conditions partially override delivery, especially for minors and public insurance. Adult emergency care exposure not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders frame gender-affirming care for minors as mutilation, direct investigation/prosecution over schools using names/pronouns, sports ban, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritising groups described as radically pro-transgender. 2025 poll: 66% support birth-sex on documents, 69% support birth-sex sports alignment.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime law covers gender identity/expression since 2001 with enhancements; 2009 first-degree murder hate-crime conviction; gay-panic defence abolished 2020; national hate-crime statute exists but only 23 units cover gender identity in state bias laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State hate-crime enforcement and anti-discrimination law protect locally, but federal threat framing and law-enforcement priorities increase outing/investigation risk at federal encounters and may chill care.

minors_guardians.exposure: National youth-care funding suspension affects state programme; November 2026 ballot measures would ban trans children from sex-aligned sports and prohibit child surgery; district sports bans adopted in 2025; federal orders target school social transition. Terms of December 2025 sports settlement undisclosed.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying law covers gender identity; 2025 act requires chosen name/pronouns in schools and any uniform option; state court ordered youth care resumed; birth-certificate/licence marker changes for minors require parent/guardian plus professional confirmation.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with minor retains state protections in state schools/care, but national funding, federal school investigations and possible ballot restrictions create unresolved exposure; state protection does not bind federal/national funding decisions.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific trans killing/violence rate against general homicide baseline is documented. National bias incidents against sexual orientation are 1/7 to 1/5 of single-bias incidents; no trans-specific traveller violence pattern documented in dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime enhancements since 2001, documented 2009 conviction, anti-discrimination law in employment, housing, public accommodations, education and credit, July 2026 assessment lists state among most protective.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police/court record shows recourse for bias crime in state, but federal custody abuse and federal investigation framing are separate exposures not remedied by state hate-crime law.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order litigation unresolved; compliance with May 2026 care injunction not sourced beyond direction to lower court; October 2026 document provisions operating status not documented; conversion-therapy amendment challenge unresolved; detention frequency for visitors unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented remedies that operate locally: consent decree, care injunction order, hate-crime conviction, facilities law and expanded anti-discrimination act. Federal remedies are partial and enjoined in part.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies do not pre-empt federal entry, federal facilities, federal custody or national funding. Unknowns concern scope of federal exposure, not absence of local protection.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that a higher-level rule (here federal/national funding and entry) can override local protective clinic/service policy and complaints may not produce timely relief. Lower than 0.35-E because this state has operating facilities access, hate-crime recourse and a court-ordered care remedy, and federal entry fraud requires four elements, not automatic exclusion.

Similar: a universal birth-sex facilities rule applies in federal buildings with courts upholding parts of the regime and no effective federal remedy, while private/state spaces may be more welcoming. Worse in custody/entry severity, better because state buildings in this jurisdiction are affirmatively protected rather than banned.

Higher than this combined case: 0.75-B has no national trans-specific entry/facility/custody restriction and local remedies with follow-up compliance. Here federal entry screening, federal facilities and federal custody conversion-model care removal remain operative exposures that state protection cannot cancel.

parsed.synthesis: In state-controlled spaces the traveller encounters strong documented protection: full facilities access, anti-discrimination coverage, hate-crime enhancements and court-backed care. The decisive exposures are federal and unavoidable at entry, in federal facilities and in federal/immigration custody, where discrepancy can lead to refusal/fraud consideration and custody can involve hormone removal or reported abuse. State law does not pre-empt those layers, and national funding already suspended state youth public-insurance coverage. Litigation and local remedies mitigate but do not remove the federal universal exposures, yielding elevated risk.
